transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main reason is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. It’s gotten to where it’s not just, you know, misplacing something small and laughing it off. I’ve missed or nearly missed heart follow-up appointments, and that scares me because those are important. Then I’ll mean to call the clinic back and somehow the whole day goes by, or a couple days, and I realize I never did it.

And even with regular things, like if I’m helping with a repair job or trying to get something fixed, I’ll show up without the right tools even though I knew what I needed before I left. It’s embarrassing, honestly. At my age people kind of expect you to forget things here and there, but this feels like it’s causing real problems, so I thought I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you been experiencing these memory problems constantly, or do they come and go?

It’s been pretty constant lately, I’d say. Not like it’s one bad week and then I’m fine for a month. The part where it’s really been causing trouble has been going on about a year and a couple months now.

It seemed to get worse after that cardiac scare I had, because I had to cut back on the walking and little projects that used to keep me kind of settled and in a routine. Since then, it’s like the forgetting has been more in my way day to day, not just an occasional slip.
Do you ever feel confused or disoriented, like you're not sure what's going on or where you are?

Not really, no. I mean, I forget what I was supposed to be doing, or I’ll walk into a room and have to stop and think, “Now what did I come in here for?” But I don’t usually feel like I don’t know where I am or what’s happening around me.

I haven’t had, like, moments where I wake up and don’t recognize the house or I’m out somewhere and can’t tell where I am. It’s more that I lose track of the thing I meant to do, if that makes sense. So confused in that “my mind dropped the thread” kind of way, maybe, but not disoriented like I don’t know where I am.
Have you been having trouble learning new things, like picking up a new hobby or understanding new instructions?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really tried to pick up a brand-new hobby or anything like that lately, so it’s hard for me to say. If someone gives me instructions, I might need them repeated or written down, but I don’t know if that’s me not learning it or just not holding onto it in the moment.

Like, if it’s something practical and someone shows me, I can usually follow along better than if they just tell me a bunch of steps all at once. But I can’t think of a clear example where I just couldn’t understand something new. It’s more… I’d have to think about that a bit.
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're trying to express something?

I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, everybody has that thing where a word is on the tip of your tongue and you’re waving your hand around trying to get it, but I haven’t really noticed it being a regular problem for me.

Sometimes I’ll pause because I’m trying to explain something in the right order, or I lose where I was going with the sentence, but it’s not like I can’t name common things or I’m using the wrong word all the time. At least, I don’t think I am. My family hasn’t really pointed that out to me either. So… no, I wouldn’t say word-finding is one of the main things I’m dealing with.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

Yes, that’s probably one of the bigger things I notice. I can start out really meaning to pay attention, you know, like I’ll sit down at the bridge table and I’m telling myself, “Okay, listen, follow what’s being played, keep track,” and then after a little while it’s like my mind just sort of slides off somewhere else. Then I come back and realize I missed half of what happened.

Same kind of thing at a Fix-It Friends planning meeting. I’ll be sitting there, looking like I’m listening, and I do want to listen, but then suddenly people are talking about something and I’m thinking, “Wait, when did we get to that?” I don’t always notice the exact moment I stopped paying attention. It’s more like I catch up afterward and realize I lost the thread. So yes, focusing for a stretch of time is definitely hard for me.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood over the past year?

Mood… I’m not sure I’d say I’ve noticed a big change, no. I mean, I have days where I’m irritated or restless or just kind of off, but I don’t know if that’s “mood” in the way you mean it, or just normal life stuff.

Over the past year, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually sad or anything like that. My wife might have a different read on it, I suppose, because sometimes other people notice things before you do, but from where I’m sitting, I haven’t had some major shift where I’m a totally different person emotionally.

I guess if anything, my mood goes up and down with what’s happening that day. If something’s frustrating, I get frustrated, and then later I’m fine. So… no clear change that I can point to.
Do you often feel unusually tired?

Unusually tired… I don’t know that I’d call it unusual, exactly. I mean, I’m 68, so I don’t expect to have the same energy I had when I was 30, you know? There are days I feel worn out, but I usually connect that to what I’ve been doing that day or how much I’ve had going on.

I haven’t really noticed a big change where I’m exhausted all the time, or where I’m sleeping constantly or can’t get through the day because I’m so tired. Sometimes I’ll sit down and feel like I could doze off, but then other times I’m fine. So I guess my answer is… not really unusually tired, no. Nothing that’s stood out to me as a major problem.
Have you noticed any changes in your personality over the past year?

Personality… hmm. I don’t think so, at least not in any big obvious way. I still feel like me, if that makes sense. I haven’t had people telling me I’m acting like a different person or anything like that.

I mean, I suppose everybody changes a little as they get older, and some days I’m more short with things than other days, but I don’t know that I’d call that a personality change. My wife might be able to give you a better answer because she sees me from the outside, but from my own point of view, I haven’t noticed some major shift over the past year. Nothing where I’d say, “Oh, that’s new, that’s not like me.”
Do you have trouble with planning or organizing tasks?

Planning or organizing tasks… I’m not sure how to answer that, exactly. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who sits down with a formal plan for everything, if that’s what you mean. I’ve never been a big “make a spreadsheet and color-code it” kind of person.

For everyday things, I mostly get by. If there’s something that has to be done, I usually sort of work my way into it rather than laying it all out step by step beforehand. Sometimes my wife is better at that kind of thing than I am, so if it’s something with a lot of moving parts, I may lean on her a bit or talk it through out loud.

But I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed some new major problem with planning or organizing. It’s more like… I have my own way of doing things, maybe not the neatest way, but it usually works well enough. So I guess, no, not trouble in a way that really stands out to me.
Have you been making decisions that seem impulsive or poor to you or others?

Impulsive or poor decisions… hmm. I’m trying to think of an example, and nothing big is coming to mind. I mean, I’ve made decisions I later thought, “Well, that wasn’t the smartest way to handle it,” but I think everybody does that.

I don’t think I’ve been doing things that other people are worried about, like making reckless choices or suddenly acting way out of character. At least no one has sat me down and said, “What are you doing?” or anything like that.

Sometimes I’ll decide something quickly just because I don’t want to keep going back and forth over it, but that doesn’t usually feel impulsive to me. It’s more like I just want the decision made. So… I’d say no, not in a way that seems unusual or poor to me. If my wife thinks differently, she might say, but from my side I haven’t noticed anything major.
Do you find yourself often having trouble remembering the names of familiar people or places?

Names of familiar people or places… no, I don’t think so, not in any regular way. I mean, I’ll have the normal thing where a name is on the tip of my tongue for a minute, especially if it’s someone I haven’t seen in a while, and then it comes back later. But familiar people, like family or neighbors I see often, I’m not blanking on who they are or anything like that.

Places, same thing. I might pause trying to remember the exact name of a restaurant or a street if I haven’t been there in ages, but I don’t feel like I’m forgetting familiar places. I still know where I’m going and what places are called, at least the ones that are part of my usual life.

So I’d say no, not something I’ve really noticed as a problem.
Have you noticed any problems with judging distances or seeing things in three dimensions?

Judging distances or seeing in three dimensions… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m trying to picture what you mean—like reaching for something and missing it, or misjudging a step, or parking the car crooked because I can’t tell where things are? I haven’t really noticed anything like that being a problem.

I do the usual older-guy stuff, you know, maybe I’m a little more careful on stairs or if the lighting is bad, but I don’t feel like the world looks flat or like I can’t tell how far away things are. If I’m pouring coffee or picking something up from the counter, I’m not missing it. And I’m not bumping into doorways or furniture because I can’t judge where they are.

So, no, nothing that stands out to me there. I haven’t had a reason to think my depth perception is off.
Did you notice your memory problems and difficulty focusing start or get worse after your cardiac scare?

Yeah… I think that’s about when it really started to become a problem. Not like I woke up the next day and suddenly everything was different, but after that cardiac scare, when I had to cut way back on the walking and the little projects I used to do, things just didn’t feel as settled.

Before that, I had a routine, you know? I’d be moving around, doing things, keeping myself occupied, and I think that helped me more than I realized. Once I wasn’t doing as much, the memory and focusing issues became harder to ignore. It’s been causing real trouble for, I’d say, about a year and two months now.

So yes, I’d connect it pretty closely with that time—not necessarily that the scare itself caused everything, but after it forced me to slow down, that’s when it got worse enough that I really noticed it.
Have you had any falls or hits to the head recently?

No, not that I can think of. I mean, I’ve had the normal little stumbles or catching my foot on something around the house, but I haven’t actually fallen to the ground or hit my head recently.

I’m trying to think if there was anything I brushed off—like bumping into a cabinet door or something—but nothing that I’d call a head injury, and nothing where I was dizzy afterward or had to get checked. So, no, I don’t think there’s been anything like that recently.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over the past year?

Changes in my sleep… hmm. I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything clear-cut over the past year. I mean, I’m 68, so sleep isn’t exactly like it was when I was younger, you know? Some nights are better than others, and sometimes I wake up and have to roll over or use the bathroom, that sort of thing, but I don’t know that I’d say there’s been some big change.

I haven’t really been keeping track of it, so it’s hard for me to say for sure. If you mean like suddenly sleeping all day, or not sleeping at all, or nightmares or something like that—no, nothing that really jumps out at me. I guess I’d say my sleep feels kind of normal for me, at least as far as I can tell.
Do you have trouble finding the right words when you're writing something?

Writing something… well, I don’t do a whole lot of writing these days, to be honest. Mostly just little notes, maybe a card, or jotting something down so I don’t forget it. I can’t say I’ve really noticed a big problem where I’m stuck trying to find a word.

I mean, sometimes I’ll pause and think, “What’s the word I want here?” but I always figured that was pretty normal. It’s not like I’m sitting there unable to write a sentence or using the wrong words all the time. So… no, I don’t think that’s been a major issue for me.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Significant weight? No, I don’t think so. I mean, my weight goes up and down a few pounds here and there, depending on how I’m eating or how much I’m moving around, but I haven’t noticed anything dramatic.

I don’t weigh myself every single day or keep a chart or anything like that, so I can’t give you an exact number. But my clothes fit about the same, and nobody’s said, “You look like you’ve lost a lot of weight,” or anything. So as far as I know, no significant weight loss recently.
Do you have trouble making decisions on your own?

Making decisions on my own… hmm. I don’t know that I’d call it “trouble,” exactly. I mean, it depends what kind of decision you mean.

If it’s something small, like what to eat or what to watch on TV, I can decide that myself, though I might go back and forth a little longer than I need to. Bigger things, I usually like to talk it over with someone, just to make sure I’m not missing something. But I think a lot of people do that, especially as you get older and you don’t want to make a mess of something.

I wouldn’t say I’m unable to make decisions on my own. I’m not just sitting there frozen all the time waiting for someone else to tell me what to do. Sometimes I second-guess myself, sure, but I don’t know if that’s unusual or if that’s just me being careful. So… no, I haven’t really noticed a major problem with that.
Have you had any head injuries or concussions in the past year?

Head injuries or concussions in the past year… no, not that I can think of. I mean, I’ve bumped my head here and there like anybody does—getting something out of a cabinet or misjudging where a shelf is—but nothing where I blacked out or had to go get checked or anything like that.

I’m trying to think back over the year, because time kind of blends together sometimes, but no, I don’t remember any fall or accident where someone said, “You might have a concussion.” So as far as I know, no head injury or concussion in the past year.
